passages.text: “You shall not spread a false report. Do not join the wicked by being a malicious witness.
passages.sermon:
God commands His people to be holy.
\r\nYou must not spread a false report.
\r\nYou must not join with wicked people.
\r\nYou must not act as a malicious witness.
passages.original: לֹ֥א תִשָּׂ֖א שֵׁ֣מַע שָׁ֑וְא אַל־ תָּ֤שֶׁת יָֽדְךָ֙ עִם־ רָשָׁ֔ע לִהְיֹ֖ת עֵ֥ד חָמָֽס׃ס

passages.text: You shall not follow the crowd in wrongdoing. When you testify in a lawsuit, do not pervert justice by siding with the crowd.
passages.sermon:
God commands His people to act justly.
Do not follow the crowd when they do wrong.
Do not join others in evil actions.
If you testify in court, speak the truth.
Do not change your testimony to agree with the majority.
Do not help others twist justice.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ תִהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרֵֽי־ רַבִּ֖ים לְרָעֹ֑ת וְלֹא־ תַעֲנֶ֣ה עַל־ רִ֗ב לִנְטֹ֛ת אַחֲרֵ֥י רַבִּ֖ים לְהַטֹּֽת׃

passages.text: And do not show favoritism to a poor man in his lawsuit.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to Israel.
God commanded judges and people.
God said, “Do not show favoritism.”
Do not favor a poor man in his lawsuit.
Treat every person fairly in court.
Do not let poverty influence your judgment.
passages.original: וְדָ֕ל לֹ֥א תֶהְדַּ֖ר בְּרִיבֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: If you encounter your enemy’s stray ox or donkey, you must return it to him.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to Israel.
God said, “If you see your enemy’s ox wandering, return it to him.”
If you find your enemy’s donkey lost, bring it back to him.
You must not ignore your enemy’s lost animal.
You must give it back to its owner.
passages.original: כִּ֣י תִפְגַּ֞ע שׁ֧וֹר אֹֽיִבְךָ֛ א֥וֹ חֲמֹר֖וֹ תֹּעֶ֑ה הָשֵׁ֥ב תְּשִׁיבֶ֖נּוּ לֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: If you see the donkey of one who hates you fallen under its load, do not leave it there; you must help him with it.
passages.sermon:
God gives a command about how to treat your enemy.
You may see a donkey.
This donkey belongs to someone who hates you.
The donkey has fallen under its load.
Do not ignore the donkey.
Do not leave the donkey there.
You must help your enemy with his donkey.
You must help lift the load with him.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תִרְאֶ֞ה חֲמ֣וֹר שֹׂנַאֲךָ֗ רֹבֵץ֙ תַּ֣חַת מַשָּׂא֔וֹ וְחָדַלְתָּ֖ מֵעֲזֹ֣ב ל֑וֹ עָזֹ֥ב תַּעֲזֹ֖ב עִמּֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: You shall not deny justice to the poor in their lawsuits.
passages.sermon:
God commands you to act justly.
\r\nDo not deny justice to the poor.
\r\nDo not treat the poor unfairly in their lawsuits.
\r\nGive the poor a fair judgment in every dispute.
passages.original: לֹ֥א תַטֶּ֛ה מִשְׁפַּ֥ט אֶבְיֹנְךָ֖ בְּרִיבֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Stay far away from a false accusation. Do not kill the innocent or the just, for I will not acquit the guilty.
passages.sermon:
God commands you to avoid lies.
Stay far away from false accusations.
Do not kill innocent people.
Do not kill just people.
God will not declare the guilty to be innocent.
passages.original: מִדְּבַר־ שֶׁ֖קֶר תִּרְחָ֑ק וְנָקִ֤י וְצַדִּיק֙ אַֽל־ תַּהֲרֹ֔ג כִּ֥י לֹא־ אַצְדִּ֖יק רָשָֽׁע׃

passages.text: Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.
passages.sermon:
God commands you.
Do not accept a bribe.
A bribe blinds people who see clearly.
A bribe twists the words of righteous people.
passages.original: וְשֹׁ֖חַד לֹ֣א תִקָּ֑ח כִּ֤י הַשֹּׁ֙חַד֙ יְעַוֵּ֣ר פִּקְחִ֔ים וִֽיסַלֵּ֖ף דִּבְרֵ֥י צַדִּיקִֽים׃

passages.text: Do not oppress a foreign resident, since you yourselves know how it feels to be foreigners; for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
God commands His people not to oppress a foreign resident.
You must not mistreat someone who lives among you but is not from your land.
You know how a foreigner feels.
You were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You experienced what it is like to be a stranger.
Therefore, do not oppress the foreign resident.
passages.original: וְגֵ֖ר לֹ֣א תִלְחָ֑ץ וְאַתֶּ֗ם יְדַעְתֶּם֙ אֶת־ נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַגֵּ֔ר כִּֽי־ גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: For six years you are to sow your land and gather its produce, but in the seventh year you must let it rest and lie fallow, so that the poor among your people may eat from the field and the wild animals may consume what they leave. Do the same with your vineyard and olive grove.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws for the land.
For six years, you must plant your fields.
You must gather the crops from your land during these six years.
In the seventh year, you must let your land rest.
You must not plant or harvest in the seventh year.
Let the poor people among you eat what grows in your fields during this year.
Let the wild animals eat what the poor people leave behind.
You must do the same with your vineyard.
You must do the same with your olive grove.
passages.original: וְשֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים תִּזְרַ֣ע אֶת־ אַרְצֶ֑ךָ וְאָסַפְתָּ֖ אֶת־ תְּבוּאָתָֽהּ׃ וְהַשְּׁבִיעִ֞ת תִּשְׁמְטֶ֣נָּה וּנְטַשְׁתָּ֗הּ וְאָֽכְלוּ֙ אֶבְיֹנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ וְיִתְרָ֕ם תֹּאכַ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה כֵּֽן־ תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לְכַרְמְךָ֖ לְזֵיתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: For six days you are to do your work, but on the seventh day you must cease, so that your ox and your donkey may rest and the son of your maidservant may be refreshed, as well as the foreign resident.
passages.sermon:
God commands you to work for six days.
You must do all your tasks during these six days.
On the seventh day, you must stop working.
You must rest on the seventh day.
Your ox must rest on the seventh day.
Your donkey must rest on the seventh day.
The son of your maidservant must be refreshed on the seventh day.
The foreign resident must also be refreshed on the seventh day.
passages.original: שֵׁ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה מַעֲשֶׂ֔יךָ וּבַיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י תִּשְׁבֹּ֑ת לְמַ֣עַן יָנ֗וּחַ שֽׁוֹרְךָ֙ וַחֲמֹרֶ֔ךָ וְיִנָּפֵ֥שׁ בֶּן־ אֲמָתְךָ֖ וְהַגֵּֽר׃

passages.text: Pay close attention to everything I have said to you. You must not invoke the names of other gods; they must not be heard on your lips.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God gives them commands and instructions.
God says, “Pay close attention to everything I have told you.”
Do not mention the names of other gods.
Do not speak their names with your mouth.
Do not let the names of other gods be heard from your lips.
passages.original: וּבְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ אָמַ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם תִּשָּׁמֵ֑רוּ וְשֵׁ֨ם אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֲחֵרִים֙ לֹ֣א תַזְכִּ֔ירוּ לֹ֥א יִשָּׁמַ֖ע עַל־ פִּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Three times a year you are to celebrate a feast to Me.
passages.sermon:
God commands His people to celebrate feasts.
God requires these feasts each year.
You must celebrate three feasts every year.
You celebrate these feasts for God.
passages.original: שָׁלֹ֣שׁ רְגָלִ֔ים תָּחֹ֥ג לִ֖י בַּשָּׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: You are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread as I commanded you: At the appointed time in the month of Abib you are to eat unleavened bread for seven days, because that was the month you came out of Egypt. No one may appear before Me empty-handed.
passages.sermon:
God commanded the Israelites to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
They must observe this feast as God instructed them.
They must celebrate it at the appointed time in the month of Abib.
They must eat unleavened bread for seven days during this time.
God chose the month of Abib because He brought the Israelites out of Egypt in that month.
No one may appear before God empty-handed.
passages.original: אֶת־ חַ֣ג הַמַּצּוֹת֮ תִּשְׁמֹר֒ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִים֩ תֹּאכַ֨ל מַצּ֜וֹת כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֗ךָ לְמוֹעֵד֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽאָבִ֔יב כִּי־ ב֖וֹ יָצָ֣אתָ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וְלֹא־ יֵרָא֥וּ פָנַ֖י רֵיקָֽם׃

passages.text: You are also to keep the Feast of Harvest with the firstfruits of the produce from what you sow in the field. And keep the Feast of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather your produce from the field.
passages.sermon:
God commanded the Israelites to keep certain feasts each year.
Keep the Feast of Harvest.
This feast uses the firstfruits of the crops you plant in your field.
Also keep the Feast of Ingathering.
This feast happens at the end of the year.
You celebrate it when you gather your produce from the field.
passages.original: וְחַ֤ג הַקָּצִיר֙ בִּכּוּרֵ֣י מַעֲשֶׂ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּזְרַ֖ע בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וְחַ֤ג הָֽאָסִף֙ בְּצֵ֣את הַשָּׁנָ֔ה בְּאָסְפְּךָ֥ אֶֽת־ מַעֲשֶׂ֖יךָ מִן־ הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: Three times a year all your males are to appear before the Lord GOD.
passages.sermon: All your males must appear before the Lord GOD.\r\nThey must do this three times each year.
passages.original: שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים בַּשָּׁנָ֑ה יֵרָאֶה֙ כָּל־ זְכ֣וּרְךָ֔ אֶל־ פְּנֵ֖י הָאָדֹ֥ן׀ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: You must not offer the blood of My sacrifices with anything leavened, nor may the fat of My feast remain until morning.
passages.sermon: God gave instructions for sacrifices and feasts.\r\nDo not offer the blood of God's sacrifices with anything leavened.\r\nDo not let the fat from God's feast remain until morning.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ תִזְבַּ֥ח עַל־ חָמֵ֖ץ דַּם־ זִבְחִ֑י וְלֹֽא־ יָלִ֥ין חֵֽלֶב־ חַגִּ֖י עַד־ בֹּֽקֶר׃

passages.text: Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God. You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.
passages.sermon:
God commands the people of Israel.
God tells them to bring the best of the firstfruits from their land.
They must bring these firstfruits to the house of the LORD their God.
God also gives another command.
They must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.
passages.original: רֵאשִׁ֗ית בִּכּוּרֵי֙ אַדְמָ֣תְךָ֔ תָּבִ֕יא בֵּ֖ית יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹֽא־ תְבַשֵּׁ֥ל גְּדִ֖י בַּחֲלֵ֥ב אִמּֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: Behold, I am sending an angel before you to protect you along the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God says, “I am sending an angel ahead of you.”
This angel will protect you as you travel.
This angel will lead you.
He will bring you to the place I have prepared for you.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י שֹׁלֵ֤חַ מַלְאָךְ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ לִשְׁמָרְךָ֖ בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ וְלַהֲבִ֣יאֲךָ֔ אֶל־ הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲכִנֹֽתִי׃

passages.text: Pay attention to him and listen to his voice; do not defy him, for he will not forgive rebellion, since My Name is in him.
passages.sermon:
God is sending an angel before you.
This angel protects you on your journey.
This angel brings you to the place God has prepared.
Pay attention to this angel.
Listen to his voice.
Do not defy him.
He will not forgive your rebellion.
God’s Name is in him.
passages.original: הִשָּׁ֧מֶר מִפָּנָ֛יו וּשְׁמַ֥ע בְּקֹל֖וֹ אַל־ תַּמֵּ֣ר בּ֑וֹ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִשָּׂא֙ לְפִשְׁעֲכֶ֔ם כִּ֥י שְׁמִ֖י בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But if you will listen carefully to his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God sends an angel before them.
God says, "If you listen carefully to the angel's voice,
and if you do everything I command,
then I will be an enemy to your enemies.
I will oppose those who oppose you."
passages.original: כִּ֣י אִם־ שָׁמֹ֤עַ תִּשְׁמַע֙ בְּקֹל֔וֹ וְעָשִׂ֕יתָ כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲדַבֵּ֑ר וְאָֽיַבְתִּי֙ אֶת־ אֹ֣יְבֶ֔יךָ וְצַרְתִּ֖י אֶת־ צֹרְרֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: For My angel will go before you and bring you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will annihilate them.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God said He would send His angel ahead of them.
God’s angel would go before the Israelites.
The angel would lead the Israelites into the land.
This land belonged to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
God said He would destroy these nations.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יֵלֵ֣ךְ מַלְאָכִי֮ לְפָנֶיךָ֒ וֶהֱבִֽיאֲךָ֗ אֶל־ הָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַ֣חִתִּ֔י וְהַפְּרִזִּי֙ וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִ֑י וְהִכְחַדְתִּֽיו׃

passages.text: You must not bow down to their gods or serve them or follow their practices. Instead, you are to demolish them and smash their sacred stones to pieces.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God gave them commands about the nations in the land.
Do not bow down to the gods of those nations.
Do not serve their gods.
Do not follow their practices.
Destroy their gods completely.
Break their sacred stones into pieces.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֤ה לֵאלֹֽהֵיהֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א תָֽעָבְדֵ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תַעֲשֶׂ֖ה כְּמַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם כִּ֤י הָרֵס֙ תְּהָ֣רְסֵ֔ם וְשַׁבֵּ֥ר תְּשַׁבֵּ֖ר מַצֵּבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: So you shall serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water. And I will take away sickness from among you.
passages.sermon:
You must serve the LORD your God.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
He will bless your bread.
He will bless your water.
He will remove sickness from among you.
passages.original: וַעֲבַדְתֶּ֗ם אֵ֚ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵרַ֥ךְ אֶֽת־ לַחְמְךָ֖ וְאֶת־ מֵימֶ֑יךָ וַהֲסִרֹתִ֥י מַחֲלָ֖ה מִקִּרְבֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: No woman in your land will miscarry or be barren; I will fulfill the number of your days.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God promised to bless the people in their land.
No woman in your land will miscarry.
No woman in your land will be barren.
I, the LORD, will give you a full life.
I will complete the number of your days.
passages.original: לֹ֥א תִהְיֶ֛ה מְשַׁכֵּלָ֥ה וַעֲקָרָ֖ה בְּאַרְצֶ֑ךָ אֶת־ מִסְפַּ֥ר יָמֶ֖יךָ אֲמַלֵּֽא׃

passages.text: I will send My terror ahead of you and throw into confusion every nation you encounter. I will make all your enemies turn and run.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God promised to help them as they entered new lands.
God said, “I will send My terror ahead of you.”
I will confuse every nation you meet.
I will make all your enemies turn their backs and run away from you.
passages.original: אֶת־ אֵֽימָתִי֙ אֲשַׁלַּ֣ח לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְהַמֹּתִי֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּבֹ֖א בָּהֶ֑ם וְנָתַתִּ֧י אֶת־ כָּל־ אֹיְבֶ֛יךָ אֵלֶ֖יךָ עֹֽרֶף׃

passages.text: I will send the hornet before you to drive the Hivites and Canaanites and Hittites out of your way.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God promised to help them enter the land.
God said, "I will send the hornet ahead of you."
The hornet will go before you.
The hornet will drive out the Hivites.
The hornet will drive out the Canaanites.
The hornet will drive out the Hittites.
These nations will leave before you.
passages.original: וְשָׁלַחְתִּ֥י אֶת־ הַצִּרְעָ֖ה לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וְגֵרְשָׁ֗ה אֶת־ הַחִוִּ֧י אֶת־ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֛י וְאֶת־ הַחִתִּ֖י מִלְּפָנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: I will not drive them out before you in a single year; otherwise the land would become desolate and wild animals would multiply against you.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God promised to remove their enemies from the land.
God said, “I will not drive them out before you in a single year.
If I remove them all at once, the land will become empty.
If the land becomes empty, wild animals will increase against you.”
passages.original: לֹ֧א אֲגָרְשֶׁ֛נּוּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ בְּשָׁנָ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת פֶּן־ תִּהְיֶ֤ה הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ שְׁמָמָ֔ה וְרַבָּ֥ה עָלֶ֖יךָ חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: Little by little I will drive them out ahead of you, until you become fruitful and possess the land.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God promised to help them.
God said, “I will drive your enemies out from before you.”
I will not remove them all at once.
I will drive them out little by little.
I will do this until you grow in number.
I will do this until you become fruitful.
Then you will take possession of the land.
passages.original: מְעַ֥ט מְעַ֛ט אֲגָרְשֶׁ֖נּוּ מִפָּנֶ֑יךָ עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּפְרֶ֔ה וְנָחַלְתָּ֖ אֶת־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: And I will establish your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the desert to the Euphrates. For I will deliver the inhabitants into your hand, and you will drive them out before you.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God promised to set their borders.
God said the borders would go from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines.
God said the borders would go from the desert to the Euphrates River.
God said He would give the people living in the land into the Israelites’ power.
God said the Israelites would drive out these people from before them.
passages.original: וְשַׁתִּ֣י אֶת־ גְּבֻלְךָ֗ מִיַּם־ סוּף֙ וְעַד־ יָ֣ם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּמִמִּדְבָּ֖ר עַד־ הַנָּהָ֑ר כִּ֣י׀ אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּיֶדְכֶ֗ם אֵ֚ת יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ וְגֵרַשְׁתָּ֖מוֹ מִפָּנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: You shall make no covenant with them or with their gods.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God commanded the Israelites.
Do not make a covenant with the people living in the land.
Do not make a covenant with their gods.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ תִכְרֹ֥ת לָהֶ֛ם וְלֵאלֹֽהֵיהֶ֖ם בְּרִֽית׃

passages.text: They must not remain in your land, lest they cause you to sin against Me. For if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God warned them about the people living in the land.
God said, “They must not stay in your land.
If they stay, they might lead you to sin against Me.
If you serve their gods, you will fall into a trap.
Their gods will become a snare to you.”
passages.original: לֹ֤א יֵשְׁבוּ֙ בְּאַרְצְךָ֔ פֶּן־ יַחֲטִ֥יאוּ אֹתְךָ֖ לִ֑י כִּ֤י תַעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־ אֱלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־ יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֖ לְמוֹקֵֽשׁ׃פ
